clue.text: One rotten actor is spoiling TV series

indicators.note: spoiling means ruining, so the four words before it are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A long-running TV show is being dragged down by one terrible performer in its cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiling' is the anagram signal on all sixteen letters of ONE ROTTEN ACTOR IS. The result is the name of Britain's longest-running TV soap opera, set in a fictional Manchester district.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-running British soap opera on ITV, so an example of a television series.

clue.text: Reportedly dispose of part of prison

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken or heard, so the word given sounds like the entry

parts.note: to dispose of goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone appears to have heard rumours of a prison wing being sold off.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's small room is a basic unit of a jail building, so it forms part of it.

clue.text: Answer some correspondence

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters are taken from within the following word

explanation.surface: An instruction to reply to a few of the letters in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to reply to someone or something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Evidently women only troubled at cruel name-calling?

parts.note: a group that is women only clearly has no men

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A women-only gathering is apparently upset by cruel insults being hurled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evidently women only' gives NO MEN, which joins AT CRUEL as fodder for the anagram signalled by 'troubled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A system for naming things is literally the calling of names, the question mark flagging the playful reading of an insult idiom.

clue.text: Listen: a city-dweller will show resolve

indicators.note: will show means will reveal, so the letters are displayed inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An urban resident is told to pay attention and demonstrate determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'lisTEN A CITY-dweller', ignoring the punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun is firmness of purpose, the same as stubborn persistence.

clue.text: Choice of fostering when Bill leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the bill's letters are removed from the word

parts.note: fostering a cause or a child can be called adopting it
AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A man called Bill walks out, leaving his partner to decide about taking in a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean something one may select, an alternative open to choose.

clue.text: Actor Johnny, almost swallowing ecstasy, becomes profound

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the drug's letter goes within
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the surname is dropped

parts.note: Johnny Depp is the American film actor
E is the common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star takes a drug and turns philosophical.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep thoughts are profound ones; the adjectives are synonyms for intellectual depth.

clue.text: Inflammatory reason to support English

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a motive is the reason for doing something

explanation.surface: Something provocative is offered as a justification for backing the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammatory words stir up strong feeling, which is what charged, feeling-rousing language does.

clue.text: Scheme and lie about getting shot, possibly

parts.note: a scheme is a planned undertaking, a project

indicators.note: about here means around in a jumbled way, signalling a rearrangement of the word lie

explanation.surface: Someone plots and fibs their way out of trouble after a shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot such as a bullet or cannonball is one example of a missile fired through the air.

clue.text: Just in time, survive with very little

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means tiny

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes by on almost nothing and only just makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the final moment before a deadline is done only just in time.

clue.text: Fly very near the ground? Not quite

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: low means close to the ground

explanation.surface: A question about whether an aircraft is skimming dangerously close to the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like part of the low-flying picture but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly without an instructor or companion is to make an unaccompanied flight, a pilot's sense of the verb.

clue.text: Life-saving treatment needed where estuaries meet?

definitions.meaning: rescue breathing given by pressing lips together to inflate a casualty's lungs
an estuary is a river's mouth, so two meeting would be placed lip to lip, the question mark marking the whimsy

explanation.definitionFit: It is the resuscitation technique of breathing into a victim's lungs; literally, two openings pressed together.

clue.text: Express disapproval of new gift

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a fresh present they have been given.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something given that is welcome, like a present.

clue.text: One's snappy seeing cool cider being drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means in a muddled state, so the letters of cool cider are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets irritable while downing chilled cider.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile snaps its jaws, so it is literally a snappy creature, a playful description.

clue.text: See 21
Mostly unnecessary and overdue wave

indicators.note: mostly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: undue means excessive or unwarranted
late means overdue, after the expected time

explanation.surface: A wave that is largely needless and has also arrived behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean to move in a rippling, rising and falling motion.

clue.text: See 1
Cures seem dire somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters of seem dire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Treatments for illness appear dreadful in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cures and treatments that put things right are synonyms, both plural nouns.

clue.text: Leading Russian swapping parts before son enters

indicators.note: before places the one piece ahead of the next
swapping parts means the two halves of the name change places

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian leader

explanation.surface: The Russian president moves pieces around before his son comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the definition, a verb, as in keying data into a computer. Splitting the surname into PUT and IN and swapping them gives the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To key data into a computer is to feed it in, so the verbs share this computing sense.

clue.text: Plan for retirement?

parts.note: a scheme that pays an income after one stops working, the question mark flagging a deliberately plain description

explanation.definitionFit: It is the regular payment drawn after leaving work, typically arranged through a savings scheme.

clue.text: Article must be rewritten by five, straight up!

indicators.note: by means next to, so the numeral sits beside the rearranged word

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: rewritten means written out again in a new order, so the letters of article are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor insists a piece be redone by five o'clock, no messing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rising straight up is perpendicular to the ground, the geometric sense.

clue.text: HANGING?

parts.note: the word is printed in upper-case letters, and hanging is a penalty of death; the question mark flags the double reading

explanation.definitionFit: Hanging is a form of execution, the death penalty; the clue is also literally written in block letters.

clue.text: Trendy, like old colour

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: A shade that is fashionable and also retro.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a deep blue-violet dye and hue, one of the seven colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Exotic dancer seen by husband in bar

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, so the pieces stand next to one another
exotic means unusual or foreign, so the letters of dancer are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is spotted by a husband in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the setting of the scene, but it is the definition, meaning an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar in the sense of an obstruction is something that gets in the way, a synonym.

clue.text: Cleaning equipment shocks?

definitions.meaning: floor-cleaning tools with a head of absorbent strands on a long handle
shocks of hair are thick untidy masses

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both floor-cleaning tools and thick, tousled heads of hair.

clue.text: They're handy when fighting members

definitions.meaning: weapons are useful to have in a battle
limbs of the body are called members

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a unit come in useful in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weapons and the upper limbs, which end in hands.

clue.text: Give out what's said to be money, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the proverb says time is money

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, someone hands out what is proverbially worth cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out light, heat or sound is to discharge it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Delaying tactic from one coach overcome by strain

indicators.note: overcome by means covered or swallowed up, so the pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: to strain liquid is to filter it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A coach overwhelmed by stress is used to stall for time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the parliamentary tactic of making very long speeches to delay or block a vote.

clue.text: Beat king's war machine

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A defeated monarch's military vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an armoured fighting vehicle on tracks, a machine built for battle.

clue.text: Families keep being taken in by star signs

indicators.note: taken in means enclosed, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: in astrology the zodiac is divided into twelve houses
to keep something is to hold it

explanation.surface: Families keep getting fooled by horoscopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived by astrology, but here it means contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A household is a family or group living together under one roof, so the plurals match.
